item.title: Climate Week NYC Kicks off With World Leaders’ Commitments to Action
item.description: The Climate Group’s annual conference in New York City has attracted thousands of attendees this year, among them world leaders, corporate heads, philanthropists, and climate advocates. Those leaders present at the opening ceremony of Climate Week have made clear calls to collectively tackle climate issues. Climate Week NYC’s opening ceremony and conference began on Monday […]

item.title: Displacement on the rise in Yemen as fighting continues
item.description: As hostilities worsen in Yemen, more people have been fleeing their homes, further intensifying the humanitarian crisis within the region, the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) warned on Tuesday.

item.title: Trump defends military action against Iran, Venezuela, and calls for rebrand of AI
item.description: US President Donald Trump used his address to the UN General Assembly on Tuesday to defend recent military action against Iran, urging countries to maintain economic pressure on Tehran – and declaring that he now faces a choice between making a deal, or taking far more drastic steps.

item.title: Diplomacy is the way to address global challenges, Brazil tells General Assembly
item.description: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva told the General Assembly on Tuesday that the UN needs to become a “temple of peace” once again, as it confronts one of the most critical periods in its 80-year history.

item.title: Time to accept ‘hard truths’ so trust can be rebuilt: General Assembly president
item.description: The UN’s survival for 80 years is not, by itself, proof of success, and now, the institution must confront painful truths if it hopes to rebuild public trust, said Khalilur Rahman, president of the General Assembly’s 81st session on Tuesday.

item.title: Guterres: ‘Cracks have become canyons’ as world faces four tests of power
item.description: Humanity faces four defining “tests of power” – around war or peace, inequality, climate change and AI – that will determine whether the world moves towards a new era of cooperation or deeper division, the UN chief warned the General Assembly on Tuesday.

item.title: Millions of children return to schools that still can’t provide clean water or a working toilet
item.description: A new academic year is underway in many countries across the world, yet millions of children still attend schools where the water is unsafe to drink, toilets are unusable and there is nowhere to properly wash their hands.

item.title: Qatar: Absence of a regional collective security system is fuelling crisis in the Gulf
item.description: The crisis in the Gulf should come as a surprise to no one, the Emir of Qatar, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani said on Tuesday, describing it as the cumulative result of years of delay, crisis management through temporary fixes, and unrealistic policies.

item.title: UN rendered unable to fulfil its mission, Turkish President laments before world leaders
item.description: The United Nations continues to be weakened, and those who have tied their hopes to the world body – from Palestine to Sudan – have been disappointed, Türkiye’s President said, while adding that his country is committed to restoring confidence in the Organization.

item.title: ‘Ask us first’: Children demand a voice on AI’s future
item.description: The first generation to grow up with AI may also be the last one anyone thinks to ask about it – and that has to change, the UN's top human rights official said on Tuesday.

item.title: ‘Time is running out’ for Israel-Palestine two-State solution
item.description: The UN chief warned on Tuesday that the two-State solution for the Israel-Palestine conflict is at risk of collapse amid illegal Israeli settlement expansion and annexation.

item.title: Choose international order over ‘law of the jungle’, urges Macron
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron said on Tuesday that the world faces a stark choice: “Do we want to live…with a return to the law of the jungle – or do we want to live in a civilized international society?”

item.title: Declining Marriage and Increasing Cohabitation
item.description: Marriage is declining in many countries, with fewer people marrying and many postponing marriage until later in life. item.description: In the remote Highlands region of Papua New Guinea (PNG), humanitarians are life-saving beacons to women and girls facing myriad forms of violence. item.title: Africa Has the Technology to Achieve Food Security—Now It Needs Coordinated Deployment
item.description: Africa is emerging as the world’s fastest-growing technology market, with its innovation ecosystem attracting increasing global investment. The European Investment Bank’s recent €40 million commitment to the sector underscores this growing confidence. However, this surge in technological innovation has yet to address some of the continent’s most persistent challenges – hunger, food insecurity, and poverty. […]
